one_month_reasoning: Nothing Adobe-specific falls between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-30. Q4 FY26 results are expected around Dec 9, Adobe MAX runs Nov 10-12 and the CEO handover is Dec 1. Wadhwani's exit took effect Sep 27, so it is already public and priced. Figma's Q3 print, my main value-chain read-through, is expected Nov 4-11, just outside the window. In the window: the Oct 28 FOMC, where hike odds fell to ~35-37% after the soft Aug PCE, which helps rate-sensitive software; late-October mega-cap and software earnings with AI-capex and seat commentary; and Treasury-yield moves, which drove the late-September software weakness. ADBE fell ~19% from ~$291 on Aug 28 to ~$235 on Sep 25. Momentum points down and short-term reversal points up, so I treat them as roughly cancelling. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$238.5 with ~11.5% monthly vol (41%/3.5) and a 15% fat-tail component.

bear.story: The Dec 9 FY27 guide under a new CEO, an interim CFO and no Creative head resets to ~6-7% organic ARR growth. Value-chain evidence keeps running against Adobe: Figma compounds at 40%+, Canva's in-house models cut its AI costs ~90% and it reaccelerates toward a 2027 IPO, and model vendors absorb generic image and video creation. FY28 EPS ~$27 and the multiple slides to ~6.2x NTM (~12-13% after-SBC FCF yield). The buyback cushions per-share numbers but does not stop the de-rating.

base.story: Organic ARR growth settles at ~8%. Net new ARR declines ease, as the Q4 guide implies (-16% y/y vs -37% in Q3). The FY27 guide lands near consensus ($27-27.7) and the ~7%/yr share shrink keeps EPS growing ~10-11%. Enterprise (GenStudio/CX Enterprise with all five agency holdcos) offsets Creative seat pressure. The multiple stays around 8.7x NTM EPS of ~$29.2.

bull.story: MAX (Nov 10-12) and the new CEO land well: Firefly and freemium conversion stabilise organic ARR at ~10%. Canva's AI cost problem and a Figma deceleration show that AI-native rivals face the same economics, and software rotates back in as yields ease. ~11.5x on ~$30 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$175, ADBE would trade ~6.3x FY27 consensus EPS ($27.67) and ~12.5% after-SBC FCF yield on today's ~389M shares, below the 52-week low of $190 even as ~$2.2B/qtr of buybacks shrink the count ~7%/yr. That price would most likely mean earnings power itself is being cut, not just the multiple. Examples: a December FY27 guide from the new leadership implying low-single-digit organic ARR growth or a margin reset, or hard evidence of Creative Cloud seat losses to Canva, Figma or AI-native tools. I raised it from $170 because the extra leadership turnover (Wadhwani's exit) makes a fundamental reset in December more plausible, so a break sooner means more.

reasoning: Industry lane, round 2. The supervisor found errors in my valuation mechanics, not my industry read, and I accept them. First, my ~385M share count was stale: the 10-Q cover shows 389.2M on Sep 18, and ~$2.2B/qtr of buybacks takes it to ~360-365M by Sep 2027. Second, my FCF leg was pre-SBC at 10% and built in no growth (FY27E $10.8B = TTM CFO). After-SBC FCF is ~$8.47B TTM, and the stock yields ~9.1% on it today, so my 10% pre-SBC yield implicitly assumed a re-rating. Third, Adobe's FY ends late November, so NTM EPS at Sep 2027 is ~2/12 FY27 + 10/12 FY28 (~$29.6 at consensus), not 1/4 + 3/4. I keep a deliberate ~1.5% haircut to consensus (NTM $29.2). The reason is Wadhwani's resignation effective Sep 27: the head of Creativity & Productivity leaving before the Dec 9 guide, plus Q3 organic net new ARR -37%, is guide-reset risk that consensus has not fully absorbed. I am not stacking a big multiple cut on top: 9.25x is slightly above today's ~8.8x. Fair value moves from $275 to $270: P/E $270 (60%) and after-SBC FCF $268 (40%). The corrections largely offset. The lower share count raises per-share values, while deducting SBC and dropping the implied re-rating lowers them. Lane follow-up: Canva's figures (~$4B annualized revenue, 265M MAU, 31M paid) are now traced to the COO via TechCrunch rather than Backlinko. The 30%-to-20% growth cut on AI costs is well corroborated. Canva also claims ~90% lower AI serving costs through in-house models, so its cost disadvantage may be temporary, a mild negative for Adobe's relative position. Figma's Q3 print (Nov 4-11) is the next value-chain read-through. The stock fell ~19% in the month to Sep 25 on yields and AI-disruption rotation, which tells me not to centre on fair value. I keep the median below fair value at ~$247 (slightly under round 1's $250 for the leadership gap). The ladder is an 85/15 mix of lognormals with sigma 0.36 and 0.62, with the far upper tail trimmed. Scenarios are 25/50/25 at $165/$255/$345, a mean of ~$255. The 1-month ladder is near-symmetric around spot because there is no Adobe event in the window. Research this round: 3 searches and 1 fetch.
